q-36908.name: Question 1
q-36908.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 \\ 12 & 5\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ \\ -3 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the second column of the matrix $P.$
q-36908.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ 

Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Computing $A-(-1)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & -2 \\ 12 & 5\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ 12 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 0 \\ 12 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].$

q-36929.name: Question 2
q-36929.problem:
Determine if the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
q-36929.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is triangular, the eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal. 

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=4.$ Since we get one repeated eigenvalue, the matrix might not be diagonalizable. To check this, we row-reduce the matrix $(A-4I)\text{x}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has only $1$ pivot column. This implies that we will have only $2-1=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the current eigenvalue. Therefore, $A$ is not diagonalizable.

q-80372.name: Question 3
q-80372.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ -4 & -6\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
q-80372.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns:

Consider the matrix A=[68−4−6]. You're given that λ1=2 and λ2=−2 are the eigenvalues of A, and v1=[2−1], v2=[−11] are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices P and D such that PDP−1=A, where D is a diagonal matrix.

a
D=[02−20] and P=[2−11−11]
b
D=[2−200] and P=[21−1−1]
c
D=[02−20] and P=[2−1−11]
d
D=[−2002] and P=[21−11]
e
D=[200−2] and P=[2−1−11]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are λ1=2 and λ2=−2, we construct the diagonal matrix D by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

D=[200−2].

Now, to construct the matrix P, we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns:

  • the 1st column is the eigenvector corresponding to λ1=2, and

  • the 2nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to λ2=−2.

Therefore, we get

P=[2−1−11].

q-80493.name: Question 4
q-80493.problem:
Given the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]$, 
find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}AP.$
q-80493.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix. Since matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal: 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=-3\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-3)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $2$nd one). Thus, ${x}_{1}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a homogeneous system of linear equations with the matrix as above. Note, the matrix is already in row echelon form. There is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

q-80496.name: Question 5
q-80496.problem: Find matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=B,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix and $B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 3 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}].$
q-80496.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.** We need to find the eigenvalues of the matrix $B$ using its characteristic equation $det(B-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-5-\lambda  & 3 \\ -6 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-5-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-3\cdot (-6) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -2 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $B$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $B.$

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 3 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 0 \\ -6 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$  Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 3 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ -6 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ -6 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
